lessons: All checks passed and the production wiring, durable holds, lifecycle identity and CLI paths are accepted. Keep the current design. Fix only the one review finding in tests/test_daemon_composition.py.

test_main_drain_routes_control_after_inflight_work_and_before_the_next_offer orders pause, then resume, with asyncio.sleep(0.05). If both requests land in one inbox snapshot, consume() decides the release stale against the pre-pause releasable set, and the test hangs.

Publish the resume from a deterministic signal that the pause was applied. Inject a sleep into _control_factory (its sleep parameter) through the drain's public control_factory path, and publish the resume on its first call, when the drain is provably paused.
An alternative is to poll the journal for the pause's control_hold event before publishing the release. Either way, remove all wall-clock ordering from the test.
Make the test fail instead of hanging. clock=lambda: NOW never advances, so the admission ceiling is never reached. Use an advancing clock or an asyncio.wait_for bound so a stuck pause fails fast.

Do not change squatch/control.py consume semantics to paper over the race. The snapshot-before-hold rule is the tested pre-hold-release contract. Run `uv run pytest -q` to completion before claiming success.
